key_insight: This obstetric AI study—not cancer drug discovery research—uses time-to-event models to predict imminent delivery with fetal acidosis without assuming delivery timing is known.
clinical_relevance: Predicting acidemic delivery during labor could support earlier recognition of fetal risk, but clinical benefit remains unproven.
method: Analyze continuous fetal heart rate and contraction signals.
Adapt deep discrete-time survival models and marked point processes to partially observed acidosis labels.
Jointly predict delivery timing and fetal acidosis.
evidence_signal: Marked DeepHit predicted acidemic delivery within one hour with test AUROCs of 0.837 (95% CI 0.692–0.970) at 6 hours and 0.935 (0.858–0.964) at 12 hours into labor; the study also reports external validation at a second site.
watch_item: These proof-of-principle results require prospective evaluation before clinical implementation.
paper_title: Deep Time-to-Event Models for Intrapartum Fetal Monitoring
